Location: 	Bardon, QLD, 4065 
Full-Time: 	Immediate Start 
Job Title: 	Community Worker 
Salary Range: 	$79,500 - $85,000 | depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.  
Job Closes Date: 	30 Days   
 
About the Role 
Our client delivers person-centered support that helps individuals live independently at home and stay connected to their community. As their Community Worker, you will empower clients – including seniors, people with disabilities, and those with complex needs – to achieve their goals and participate fully in community life. 
 
Key Responsibility and Duties 
Client assessment and planning 
• Conduct holistic assessments of each client’s physical, emotional, and social needs, identifying strengths and barriers to independence. 
• Develop, implement, and regularly review individualized support, training, and educational programs that align with client goals and NDIS/aged-care plans. 
 
Client support and progress monitoring 
• Interview the clients to understand the nature and extent of their difficulties, then provide direct support or skill-building to resolve social, emotional, and financial challenges. 
• Monitor client progress through regular check-ins and documented observations, reporting outcomes to the care team, family, and funding bodies. 
 
Community engagement and referrals 
• Assess local community needs and available resources for health, housing, employment, training, and social activities, then connect clients to relevant services. 
• Liaise with community groups, welfare agencies, government bodies, and businesses to promote awareness of support services and advocate for client access. 
 
Program development and administration 
• Prepare detailed submissions for funding, resources, and program extensions, along with progress reports for government and referring agencies. 
• Supervise and support clients on probation, parole, or in adult service units, group housing, or government institutions – ensuring compliance and rehabilitation goals. 
 
Requirements 
• 1 year of full-time work experience within community services, social work, or in related positions. 
• Relevant qualifications are required. 
• Strong assessment, communication, and advocacy skills. 
• Ability to work with vulnerable populations and maintain professional boundaries. 
• Current driver’s license and willingness to travel across Brisbane. 
 
Apply now  
• This role directly contributes to meaningful, lasting changes in people’s lives. 
 
Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Location: Balaklava, SA, 5461
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Aged Care Facility Manager
Job Title: Personal Care Assistant
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role
On behalf of our client, an independent, not-for-profit aged care provider known as “the heart of country care,” we are seeking a compassionate Personal Care Assistant. Our client proudly supports older South Australians in regional communities with safe, caring, and inclusive living environments across residential aged care and retirement living. They are passionate about developing respectful, warm, and genuine relationships where everyone is valued and everyone matters. We are looking for a Personal Care Assistant who will deliver quality care through mutual respect in a warm, caring country environment, empowering residents to make choices about their life, support, and care.

Key Duties (paraphrased & detailed)
Resident-Centred Personal Care & Support
• Deliver high-quality personal care including gentle assistance with bathing, showering, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility support (transfers, walking), always following each resident’s individual care plan.
• Promote independence and dignity by encouraging residents to participate in daily activities at their comfort level, supporting them to maintain skills and choice.
• Provide emotional support and genuine companionship, engaging residents in meaningful conversations, reminiscence activities, and recreational pursuits that combat loneliness.

Specialised Care & Health Monitoring
• Assist with specialised care needs including dementia support (using calm, reassuring communication), palliative care (comfort-focused assistance), and behavioural interventions under the guidance of registered nurses.
• Observe and report any changes in residents’ physical or emotional condition (e.g., skin integrity, mood swings, appetite loss) to senior staff in a timely manner.
• Accurately document care provided and contributed to care plan reviews, ensuring resident needs are continuously met and their preferences respected.

Wellness Programs & Therapy Support
• Support therapy and wellness programs by assisting with gentle exercises (range of motion, seated stretching), cognitive stimulation activities (puzzles, memory games), and social outings within the local community.
• Encourage resident participation in group activities that foster connection and engagement, aligned with the “heart of country care” ethos.

Safety, Compliance & Environmental Care
• Adhere strictly to infection control protocols (hand hygiene, PPE use), workplace health & safety policies, and Aged Care Quality Standards to protect vulnerable residents.
• Maintain a clean, hazard-free environment, ensuring resident rooms, communal areas, and bathrooms meet hygiene standards and are free from trip risks.
• Participate in emergency response procedures including fire drills, evacuation support, and basic first aid interventions when required (certification preferred).

Team Collaboration, Communication & Continuous Improvement
• Build trusting relationships with residents’ families, providing empathetic updates on care and addressing concerns with professionalism and warmth.
• Work closely with nurses, allied health professionals (physiotherapists, OTs), and other care staff to ensure a holistic, person-centred approach to resident wellbeing.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by sharing feedback, participating in staff meetings, attending training sessions, and identifying self-education needs.

Skills & Experience Required
• Certificate III in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent qualification.
• Minimum 1-year full-time experience in a similar role (residential aged care preferred).
• NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (issued within last 5 years) – preferable.
• Up-to-date flu vaccination and full COVID-19 immunisation.
• Satisfactory police check with no disclosures; valid driver’s licence and own reliable transportation.
• Strong teamwork skills, compassionate communication, and a genuine commitment to long-term employment in a regional community setting.

Why Join?
Rewarding work making a real difference in seniors’ lives, ongoing training and professional development, supportive team culture with regular staff recognition, modern country facilities with quality resources, and career growth potential within a respected not-for-profit organisation.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Keshab Pty Ltd, the founding entity of the KHI Partners network, is part of a growing professional services group operating across Australia and the United Kingdom. KHI Partners comprises more than 30 Partners, 13+ Australian offices and provides Accounting & Tax, Bookkeeping, Financial Planning, Mortgage Broking, Legal, Buyers Agency and Insurance Broking services through its specialist partner firms.

As the group's central recruitment and HR function supporting a workforce of over 150 employees, Keshab Pty Ltd is seeking a full-time Recruitment Consultant to manage end-to-end recruitment, onboarding and talent acquisition across the KHI Partners network. This role offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to workforce planning and recruitment strategy within a dynamic and expanding professional services organisation.

Key responsibilities

-	Manage end-to-end recruitment across multiple entities within the KHI Partners Group including job design, advertising, sourcing, screening, interviewing and onboarding.
-	Develop and implement a group-wide recruitment and onboarding framework to ensure uniformity in processes and compliance with employment standards.
-	Partner with partners and practice heads to understand staffing requirements and deliver effective recruitment solutions.
-	Conduct reference and background checks, manage pre-employment screening and maintain recruitment documentation.
-	Track performance progress and gather staff feedback to support talent retention and workforce engagement initiatives.
-	Build and maintain candidate pipelines, develop relationships with external providers and industry associations.
-	Prepare recruitment metrics, dashboards and progress reports for leadership and partner meetings.
-	Support employer branding, social media and professional networking initiatives to attract top talent.
-	Contribute to workforce planning and succession strategies for the wider group.

Minimum / essential requirements

-	Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in HR, Business or related discipline OR significant demonstrable recruitment experience.
-	3 years’ end-to-end recruitment experience in a professional services environment, OR 5+ years’ broader recruitment experience.
-	Strong stakeholder management skills with ability to coordinate across multiple offices and senior management levels.
-	Good working knowledge of Australian employment law, recruitment best practice, payroll and performance management principles.
-	Excellent written & verbal communication, high integrity and proven ability to handle confidential matters.

Desirable

-	Experience recruiting for accounting, finance, legal or advisory roles.
-	Experience working in a multi-office professional services firm.
-	Data-driven approach to resourcing and forecasting.

To apply, please email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted; all applications are treated as strictly confidential.
Keshab Pty Limited is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

Jigalong Community Incorporated is seeking a capable, organised and culturally respectful Office and Town Services Manager to support the Chief Executive Officer and coordinate the day-to-day delivery of office and municipal services in Jigalong Community.

This is a full-time, fixed-term position to 30 June 2027, with any extension subject to continued funding, organisational requirements and satisfactory performance.

Salary: $72,527 per annum plus statutory superannuation and applicable district allowance.

Subsidised partly furnished accommodation is available in Jigalong. Salary packaging may also be available under JCI policy.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The position combines senior office administration, community and stakeholder liaison, governance support, visitor accommodation coordination and administration of the Remote Essential and Municipal Services program with practical oversight of municipal employees and work programs.

The successful applicant must be comfortable undertaking both office-based duties and regular field inspections, establishing priorities, maintaining accurate records, following up work and supporting local employees to deliver reliable community services.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Manage the daily operation of the JCI community office and maintain effective administrative systems, records, correspondence and work schedules.

• Act as a principal contact for community members, the JCI Board, government agencies, contractors and other stakeholders.

• Support Board and community meetings, including agendas, minutes, correspondence and follow-up of actions.

• Coordinate purchasing, quotations, supplies, invoice checking, office resources, telecommunications and other administrative services.

• Administer and support REMS funding, records, reporting, inspections, field surveys and required corrective actions.

• Prepare and coordinate municipal work programs and supervise employees undertaking rubbish collection, landfill maintenance, roads and drainage, public area maintenance, vegetation control, firebreaks, airstrip maintenance and related activities.

• Maintain plant, machinery, vehicle, servicing, asset and work-completion records, including photographs and supporting evidence where required.

• Report essential-services faults and liaise with the REMS Contract Manager, regional service providers, local government and relevant agencies.

• Coordinate visitor accommodation bookings, occupancy records, cleaning arrangements and related administration.

• Train and support local employees in office practices, record keeping, safe work practices and municipal-service requirements.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

• Demonstrated experience in office administration, operations coordination, community services or a comparable role.

• Strong organisational skills and the ability to plan work, supervise employees and follow tasks through to completion.

• Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, email and electronic record keeping.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills.

• High personal integrity, sound judgement and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

• A respectful and culturally appropriate approach to living and working in a remote Aboriginal community.

• Current Australian C Class driver’s licence.

• Legal right to work in Australia.

• Capacity to obtain and maintain a satisfactory National Police Certificate and Working with Children Check.

Experience with REMS, municipal services, remote community administration, government-funded programs, staff supervision, governance support, accommodation management, asset records or local government liaison will be highly regarded.

HOW TO APPLY

Applicants must submit:
• a current résumé;
• a covering letter;
• a brief written response addressing the essential selection criteria; and
• contact details for at least two professional referees.

Applications must be submitted through Workforce Australia.

Enquiries may be directed to:

Orlando De Biasi
Chief Executive Officer
Jigalong Community Incorporated
PMB 7
Newman WA 6753

Mobile: 0427 219 132
Email:jigalongcouncil@gmail.com

Applications close at 4:00 pm AWST on Friday 7 August 2026.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply.
